## 3-Day Hiking Weather Snapshot

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg

For **2026-09-12 to 2026-09-14**, **Denver** offers warmer, much drier hiking weather. **Vancouver** is cooler and significantly wetter, which raises trail-mud and visibility risks.

## City-by-City Hiking Comparison

| City | Sep 12 High | Sep 13 High | Sep 14 High | Rain Chance | Hiking Suitability |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Denver, United States | 24°C | 26°C | 23°C | 10%, 5%, 15% | **Excellent** |
| Vancouver, Canada | 18°C | 17°C | 16°C | 60%, 70%, 50% | **Fair to Poor** |

**Recommendation: Denver**

- **Why Denver wins:** warmer daytime temps and consistently low rain chances make for safer, more comfortable trail conditions.
- **Tradeoff:** Denver may feel hotter and drier, so hydration and sun protection matter more.
- **Vancouver’s upside:** cooler temperatures are pleasant for some hikers, but the high rain odds make three straight hiking days less reliable.
- **Vancouver’s downside:** wet trails can mean slippery footing, muddy sections, and less scenic visibility.
